etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French contagieus, from Late Latin contagiosus, from contagio.

definitions.definition: (of a disease) Easily transmitted to others.

quote.citation: 1837, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], “Success”, in Ethel Churchill: Or, The Two Brides. […], volume II, London: Henry Colburn, […], →OCLC, page 75:
quote.text: The taverns of our ancestors would ill bear contrasting with the clubs of to-day; but many a gay midnight was past in the former:—midnights, whose mirth has descended even to us; half the jests, whose gaiety is still contagious; half the epigrams, whose point is yet felt, were born of those brief and brilliant hours.

quote.citation: 2000, Damon Gough (lyrics and music), “Magic in the Air”, in The Hour of Bewilderbeast, performed by Badly Drawn Boy:
quote.text: Cause love is contagious, when it's alright / Love is contagious, when it's alright / Love is alright

definitions.definition: (of a person) Having a disease that can be transmitted to another person.

quote.citation: 19th century, Zozimus (lyrics and music), “The Finding of Moses”:
quote.text: In Agypt's land contaygious to the Nile / Old Pharao's daughter went to bathe in style,
